page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor using ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 cores. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at 2.6 GHz, with a single thread per core to eliminate noisy-neighbor issues from hyperthreading. Cache distribution includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache.

Memory configuration stands at 32.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per physical core. For high-speed temporary storage, the instance bundles 950 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Network performance is anchored by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth rating. The server does not contain hardware graphics accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate well-balanced system metrics with particular strength in memory operations. In synthetic testing, uncached memory write bandwidth achieved 96.91 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier alongside a strong PassMark memory score of 2884.52. General processing remains solid with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching 13042.0 and stress-ng multi-core registering 24502.63. In specialized tests, LLM prompt processing for medium models (7B) and PassMark encryption exhibited lower relative performance, whereas clang software compilation (21146.0) and ray tracing (18346.0) remained in the middle distribution.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of this instance is driven by the energy efficiency of the Graviton ARM64 architecture combined with onboard NVMe storage, eliminating external network-attached volume overheads for ephemeral data. Tradeoffs include lack of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512 and moderate single-core speeds. The hardware design is best aligned with distributed compute workloads, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, static web serving, and database caching setups requiring low-latency local storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 16-core ARM64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz with dedicated single-threaded physical cores. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, 950 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage, and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks show prominent memory throughput, achieving 96.91 GB/sec on uncached large-block writes and a strong PassMark memory score, paired with mid-tier multi-core computing metrics such as 13042.0 in Geekbench. Without x86 vector extensions or GPU accelerators, the instance balances cost-efficient ARM compute density with low-latency local storage, making it suited for CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed batch processing, and caching layers.
